findings.summary: The R3 fix leaves two history claims in adjacent paragraphs that a reader takes as contradictory: the retained sentence says Cursor "was private to CommitDelta until M4.5", and the new sentence says "Checkpoint has constructed one since M4.0". Both are true, but in two different milestone-numbering frames, and the javadoc gives no signpost.
findings.failure_scenario: Read literally and in one frame, M4.5 is after M4.0, so the paragraph says Checkpoint constructed a class that was still private to CommitDelta. Verified against the tree: the top-level Cursor.java and Checkpoint's `new Cursor(bytes, 8)` both arrive in the same commit, 0f7f6fd `M4.0: port the sequencer and commit log onto main`, and no M4.5 commit exists on main -- M4.5 is a row from `archive/m4`, the 60 ported commits M4.0's backlog row names, so it chronologically PRECEDES the port. A reader reconstructing when the class stopped being chain-only -- which is the very question this paragraph exists to answer, and the question R3 was raised about -- gets an ordering that cannot be reconciled without opening backlog.md:129. It is minor because the M4.5 half is pre-existing prose and neither claim misstates behaviour; it is worth recording because R3's fix is what put the two in contact. Rule 11 applies: recording it in the commit body is the cheaper answer than a fifth round on this javadoc.
